name: Clipper
rootCause: According to Clipper's post-mortem, on December 1, 2024, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in a smart contract used by Clipper, manipulating the single-asset deposit and withdrawal feature. This manipulation affected the liquidity pools on the Optimism and Base networks, causing an imbalance that allowed the attacker to withdraw more assets than they had deposited. The attack resulted in a loss of approximately $457,878.

descriptions.text: According to Clipper's post-mortem, on December 1, 2024, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in a smart contract used by Clipper, manipulating the single-asset deposit and withdrawal feature. This manipulation affected the liquidity pools on the Optimism and Base networks, causing an imbalance that allowed the attacker to withdraw more assets than they had deposited. The attack resulted in a loss of approximately $457,878.

Clipper lost $450,000 on Optimism and Base on December 1, 2024, when an exploit targeted a deposit and withdrawal logic flaw in its liquidity pools. The vulnerability was in the single-token withdrawal process, not a key compromise. A logic flaw in Clipper's single-token deposit/withdrawal process allowed attackers to manipulate pool balances between actions after obtaining a valid server signature, breaking the accounting assumptions and enabling unauthorized withdrawals.

The Clipper decentralized exchange suffered a $450,000 exploit across two Ethereum layer-2 chains. Although some speculated that the issue may have been a private key leak, Clipper denied this, and instead said that an attacker had exploited a feature allowing people to make withdrawals denominated in a single token by performing swaps along with the withdrawal. Although the $450,000 theft is relatively small compared to some other crypto hacks, it represented around 6% of the total value locked on Clipper. Clipper stated they were working to trace and attempt to recover funds, and asked the hacker to contact them to potentially negotiate a return of some funds.
